earlier_scan.source_named: Srinivasavarma 1967. Descriptive study of Narikkurava dialect (grammar), unreachable. Srinivasa Varma 1970 'Vaagri boli, an Indo-Aryan language' READ in full on archive.org: contains no stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Srinivasa Varma, Govindaswamy. 1970. Vaagri Boli, an Indo-Aryan language. Annamalainagar: Annamalai University, Department of Linguistics Publication No. 21. 324 pp. (expanded version of the author's 1967 Annamalai PhD thesis 'A Descriptive Study of Narikkorava Dialect (A Grammar of va:gri:velli bo:li)')
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only
sources.note: Chapter 1 'Phonemics' (book pp. 1-27; sections 1.1 phonemes, 1.2 contrasting pairs, 1.3 allophonic distribution, 1.4 nasalization and aspiration, 1.5 distribution, 1.6 clusters, 1.7 syllabic system) read in full: nothing on stress, accent, prominence or pitch; vowels contrast in quality, quantity and nasalization. Only prosodic remark in the book is in Syntax 8.6.4 Interrogatives, p. 168: 'The intonation of the affirmative sentences is changed in such a way to transform it into an interrogative sentence without any change in the word order.' Confirms the earlier scan's finding.
